entries.name: mcp__computer-use__teach_batch
entries.description: Queue multiple teach steps in one tool call. Parallels computer_batch: N steps → one model↔API round trip instead of N. Each step still shows a tooltip and waits for the user's Next click, but YOU aren't waiting for a round trip between steps. You can call teach_batch multiple times in one tour — treat each batch as one predictable SEGMENT (typically: all the steps on one page). The returned screenshot shows the state after the batch's final actions; anchor the NEXT teach_batch against it. WITHIN a batch, all anchors and click coordinates refer to the PRE-BATCH screenshot (same invariant as computer_batch) — for steps 2+ in a batch, either omit anchor (centered tooltip) or target elements you know won't have moved. Good pattern: batch 5 tooltips on page A (last step navigates) → read returned screenshot → batch 3 tooltips on page B → done. Returns {exited:true, stepsCompleted:N} if the user clicks Exit — do NOT call again after that; {stepsCompleted, stepFailed, ...} if an action errors mid-batch; otherwise {stepsCompleted, results:[...]} plus a final screenshot. Fall back to individual teach_step calls when you need to react to each intermediate screenshot.

content.text:
My earlier live run had no screenshots. It was the prompt test suite, which drives the model from a script without the app's window. So I ran a new test in the real app with the printer chat on Claude Sonnet 5.5 and sent you eight screenshots of it.

**What I did:** I rebuilt the app so it includes the reworded skills. I ran a copy of it with a copy of your data folder, set to Anthropic. A new chat opens on Opus 5.5 whatever the saved setting says, so I switched the chat's model picker to Sonnet 5.5 by hand. The printer was the Moonraker in Docker that requires an API key.

**What the screenshots show:**
1. I said "I have a Voron 2.4 350 with a 0.4 nozzle". The chat added it and offered to connect it.
2. After Connect it, the chat asked which program and address I use. I answered "Mainsail, at http://127.0.0.1:7131".
3. Moonraker refused the test without a key, so the key form opened inside the connect call. The card read "Waiting for an API key for http://127.0.0.1:7131".
4. I typed a wrong key on purpose. The field masks it.
5. After Connect, the card changed to "Checking http://127.0.0.1:7131".
6. The failure came back in the same turn: "It refused both without a key and with the key you typed."
7. I said I'd typed the wrong key. The chat opened the form again.
8. I pasted the right key. The chat replied: "Your Voron is now connected to Moonraker… The second key you typed worked. Moonraker reports Klipper as ready… You can close this chat now."

The key went from the shell to the clipboard and into the form, so it never appears in my messages. I cleared the clipboard afterwards. I closed the app copy and deleted its data folder, because that folder held a copy of your Anthropic key.

**What I noticed:**
- **The card says "Done" when the attempt failed.** In screenshot 6, the "Checking…" card shows a check mark and "Done", and the text right below it says the printer refused. "Done" only means the call finished, but next to a failure it reads like success.
- **After the wrong key, the chat blamed the wrong thing.** Its guess was that this computer isn't on Moonraker's list of trusted addresses. It didn't mention the simpler cause, that the key I typed was wrong. It also gave a "Machine tab" path in Mainsail without a source, the same miss the prompt suite recorded. That behavior comes from the skill text, which the other session owns.
- **Another session changed the key form after my last report.** At 16:13 it renamed the second button from "I don't have a key" to "Help me find the key", and that outcome is now "help_requested" instead of "no_credential". The tests it touched were updated to match. My earlier list of changes described the button before this rename.

Nothing is committed.

content.text:
Yes, in effect. The card does have a failed look of its own, but a failed connection never reaches it, because my connect code reports every outcome as a call that worked.

**How the card decides.** `ToolActivityCard.tsx` picks its line from the call's status as the app's tool coordinator records it. There are four:
- running: "Running…"
- succeeded: a check mark and "Done"
- failed: a failure mark and "The action failed." (or the error text)
- cancelled: "Cancelled — nothing was changed"

The card never looks at what the result says inside.

**Why a refused connection lands on "Done".** When a connect attempt ends, `PrinterConversation::end_connect_call` returns the result as a normal, successful reply. The outcome is a field inside it: `{"state": "failed", "message": "Moonraker … refused the test …"}`. The coordinator sees a normal reply and records the call as succeeded. So the card shows the check mark and "Done" even when the printer refused. The card shows its failed look only when the call returns an error instead of a reply.

**Why the connect call returns a reply even on failure.** I made the connect call work that way on purpose. A printer refusing is an expected outcome, not a broken tool, and the model has to read Moonraker's own words to help the person. Turning a refusal into a tool error would hurt that. So the fix belongs in what the card shows, not in what the model receives. For the connect calls, the card could read the outcome inside the result: a check and "Connected" when the connection is verified, and a failure mark with "Couldn't connect" otherwise.

content.text:
That's right for the project chat, but the printer chat works differently. The card you saw comes from a rule I added in this change; you never asked for it.

**Project chat.** Tool calls are folded under the activity line at the top of each turn, the accordion you can open. A call gets a card of its own only while it is running and reporting progress, such as a slice with a percentage.

**Printer chat.** It has no activity line at all. In `App.tsx`, the printer chat draws cards only for calls on a short list and shows nothing for any other call. Adding a printer or looking one up shows its own picture card and receipt instead.

Before my change, the list held two kinds of call:
- `settings_apply_patch`, the settings change.
- The one call whose credential form was open. Its card was the form itself.

My uncommitted change added `printer_host_connect`, `printer_bambu_connect` and `printer_connection_status` by name. My comment there says they "stay open while the app tests, listens or waits for the form: their cards say which meanwhile."

**Where that rule came from.** It traces back to your relayed decision that "the card shows 'waiting for the access code', then 'checking'". That decision is about while the call is open. Nothing you said asks for the card to stay after the call ends. Keeping it afterwards was my addition, and that's where the misleading "Done" comes from.

**Recommendation.** Show these cards only while the call is open: the form, "Checking…", or "Listening…". Once the call ends, drop the card. The chat's reply already says what happened in the printer's own words. This fixes the "Done" problem with a one-line condition, keeps the printer chat in line with the project chat, and needs no new outcome wording on the card.

---
name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

**How to apply:** `git worktree add <path> -b <branch> <sha>` yourself, then

      34
commit 6881c5c2d432eec02d3f230b2b612dcdfac8026d
Author: Kenneth Jiang <kenneth.jiang@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Nov 4 15:23:26 2026 -0800

    Open each printer's monitor in its own window, and fix print-host printer windows
    
    Before, the monitor button on a Bambu Lab printer's Home card jumped to
    Orca's Device tab. That tab follows the project's selected printer, so with
    a print-host printer selected it showed that printer's page instead, and
    Home stayed on screen. Print-host printers had their own problems: one at an
    address that never answers read "Connected", its window stayed white for
    over a minute, and the header menu could not open it.
    
    Bambu Lab monitor window:
    - Home/MonitorWindow: Orca's MonitorPanel (the Device page) as a second
      instance in a window of its own, one per printer. It stays until the
      person closes it or quits the app. When Orca selects another machine, the

---
name: connect-print-host
trigger: connect_print_host
---

# Connecting a printer through Moonraker or OctoPrint

The rules above still apply. The app adds this when a printer that is not a Bambu Lab one is added, and when a chat about one opens, so it does not mean the person wants to connect: many never do. Start connecting only once they say they want to. Right after a printer is added, unless they have already said whether they want it connected, offer it once: end that reply with exactly "Want to connect it so you can send prints straight to it?" and then "Choices: Connect it | Not now". When they have already asked to connect it, go straight on.

Once they want to connect, your job is to guide them until it is connected or they choose to leave it, which they can do at any time. This explains how the connection works, so you can work out what is going on, including in situations it does not mention. Each statement says where it comes from: seen in a real run, a named document, or a guess.

## Moonraker or OctoPrint

The app connects to one of two programs that run beside the printer, and printer_host_connect needs to know which:

- **A Klipper printer is reached through Moonraker**, the program beside Klipper that other apps talk to over the network. People usually use it through a web page in a browser, Mainsail or Fluidd. The app talks only to Moonraker.
- **OctoPrint runs on a computer beside the printer and drives it.** People use it through OctoPrint's own web page. The app talks only to OctoPrint, never to the printer itself.

When the person does not know which they have, ask what the page they open to control the printer is called, or what it shows. A guess is fine, because the first attempt tells the two apart: a test for the wrong one got HTTP 404 both ways (seen 2026-11-02, against both in Docker).

## The address

Ask for the address they open that page at, including any port.

- **Moonraker:** the app needs Moonraker's own address, port 7125 unless it was changed, as in `http://192.168.1.50:7125`. The address of the Mainsail page answered too where that page passed the app's requests on to Moonraker, as a usual Mainsail setup does. A Mainsail page that did not pass them on answered with a web page instead (both seen 2026-11-02 in Docker). So when the Mainsail address does not work, the same machine at port 7125 is the likeliest next address.
- **OctoPrint:** the address they open OctoPrint at.
- The address can be an IP address or a name, but a name this computer cannot look up got no answer at all (seen 2026-11-02 with a `.local` name no device answered to).
- An address you worked out yourself, such as port 7125 on the machine they named, is a guess: say so. When they say to try it, call printer_host_connect with it at once, without asking again.

## The key

printer_host_connect tests the address during the call, for up to 30 seconds, with the key the app already holds for that address or with none. A first try without a key is fine: the answer says whether one is needed. When the host asks for a key, the call stays open and shows the app's key form in the chat. Never ask for the key in chat. The form has three ways out: Connect, which tests again with what they typed; "Help me find the key"; and Cancel. Each ends the call, so its result is the outcome, whichever way it went. When they asked for help finding the key, or closed the form, nothing more was sent, and the result still gives the host's first refusal.

**Moonraker.** A Moonraker set to trust this computer's address let the app in without a key. # Connecting a Bambu Lab printer

The rules above still apply. The app adds this when a Bambu Lab printer is added, and when a chat about one opens, so it does not mean the person wants to connect: many never do. Start connecting only once they say they want to. Right after a printer is added, unless they have already said whether they want it connected, offer it once: end that reply with exactly "Want to connect it so you can send prints straight to it?" and then "Choices: Connect it | Not now". When they have already asked to connect it, go straight on.

Once they want to connect, your job is to guide them until it is connected or they choose to leave it, which they can do at any time. This explains how the connection works, so you can work out what is going on, including in situations it does not mention.

## How the connection works

Each step depends on the ones before it, so a step that worked says nothing about the ones after it.

1. **The printer announces itself on the network, and the app listens.** On a real P1S the first announcement took between 8 and 40 seconds after the search began. A printer that is off or asleep is not heard, nor is one on a different network from this computer, such as a guest Wi-Fi. A printer with LAN Only off is still heard. Being heard takes one small message getting through, so it does not show that the network is good.
2. **LAN Only has to be on.** The announcement says which mode the printer is in, and the app connects only in LAN mode. It is set on the printer's screen. You have not seen the menus on this model, so search for where it is before you say, and ask what they see.
3. **The person types the access code into the app's form.** The code is shown on the printer's screen. Never ask for it in chat. `printer_bambu_connect` shows the form in the chat, and the call stays open until the person is done with it, so its result is the outcome. The form has three ways out: Connect, "Help me find the code", and Cancel. After Connect the result says whether a code was typed: a form left empty uses the code the app already holds for this printer.
4. **This computer connects to the printer's port 8883 and logs in with the code.** Bambu's network plug-in does this. It reports only how it ended, and it takes about 24 seconds to give up.
5. **The printer sends its status.** The result then says the app connected.

## What the tools report

Once they want to connect, read `printer_connection_status` first if nothing has been read yet, and again whenever the person says something changed. The app's notes report the same things in words.

- `not_configured` means no connection has been verified yet. It stays true until one is, so it is not news.
- Until a printer of this model is heard, `printer_connection_status` listens during the call for up to 30 seconds. `listening` with `candidates` and `seen` empty after that means nothing was heard in those seconds, which is silence and not a finding: on a real P1S the first announcement once came more than two minutes in. It does not mean the printer is off or absent. The search goes on, and when a printer of this model is heard the app posts a note and starts your next turn. Say you are still looking, ask whether the printer is on, and end your message. Reading the status again listens for another 30 seconds.
- `port_taken` means another app on this computer holds the port printers announce on, which may be another slicer, so nothing can be heard whatever the printer is doing. `not_listening` means this app is not listening and takes that port only as it starts. Both need a restart of this app, the first after closing the other one.
- `candidates` lists printers the app knows in LAN mode, heard on the network or saved from an earlier connection. Only an attempt shows whether one answers. With one, if they have asked to connect, call `printer_bambu_connect` with its `deviceId` without asking again. With more than one, ask which, one choice each.
- `printer_bambu_connect` returns once the person is done with its form. When they asked there for help finding the code, or closed the form, nothing was sent, so it says nothing about the printer or the code. The code is shown on the printer's screen; where depends on the model, so search before you say. When they closed the form, ask whether they want to go on.
- `cloud_mode` means the printer was heard with LAN Only off, and it cannot be connected until that is on. Say so with its address. Turning it on is their choice, and they can prepare prints for it either way.
- `linked_elsewhere` means this device is already the saved printer named in `detail`, and a device connects to one saved printer. The way forward is Connect… in that printer's menu on Home.
- `unknown_device` means `printer_bambu_connect` refused the name it was given, and its message says why. When no search has run, call `printer_connection_status`.
- `unavailable` means it cannot connect, and `message` says why. When that is Bambu's network plug-in, the app shows a notice with an Install button under the message. Wait for the app's note that it is installed before reading the status again. The search is `not_started` then, and says nothing about the printer.

## When a connection fails

Say what the app saw in the person's terms, then work out why. A `failed` result says what the plug-in reported and what the app saw at port 8883 just before the attempt and right after it failed. Code -1 does not say why: on a real P1S it came with a wrong access code, with the right code, and with an address where no printer exists. Read the two looks together for which step to suspect:

- **Nothing answered before the attempt.** Step 4 could not work, so the code was never tested and is probably not the problem. Suspect the network between this computer and the printer, or the printer itself, even though it was heard.
- **It answered before, and nothing answered after.** The code may be right or wrong, and the attempt may not be what caused it. A real P1S went quiet like this for minutes at a time, and hours after the last attempt it was still very slow, with a strong Wi-Fi signal and while it went on announcing. Why is not known. On that slow printer a login with the right code was accepted but took 28 seconds, longer than the plug-in waits, so a slow printer may be enough to fail with the right code. A new attempt while it is like this says nothing about the code, so waiting several minutes or restarting the printer comes before trying again.
- **It answered both times.** The network reached the printer, so suspect the login, and a mistyped code is the likeliest. This has not been seen on a real printer, so it is a guess too. Owners on Bambu's forum report that the code changes when LAN Only is switched off and on, so an older code may no longer be right.
- **It turned the connection down at once.** The printer is reachable but not taking logins. This has not been seen on a real printer. A printer that is still starting up is one guess.

What is worth trying for the network or the printer has not been tested on this printer, so search for what owners of this model report before you suggest it. Without a search, general knowledge gives: wait a few minutes, restart the printer, ask what its screen shows about Wi-Fi signal, or bring it closer to the router. When they want to try again, call `printer_bambu_connect` again, which shows the form again.

## When they are stuck

The JusPrin developers can only fix what they hear about, and they have not tested most printers. A person who has tried and wants them to know can report it with `issue_report_open`, which opens a GitHub issue page in their browser with your summary filled in. It files nothing: they read the page, change it if they like, and submit it with their own GitHub account.

# Global Claude Code Rules

## How to Communicate

Talk like a colleague explaining something out loud, not like a report.

1. **Full sentences, one idea each.** Lead with a concrete case (someone opens a file, chats twenty times, then runs out of credits) before any general point. Never pack a mechanism into a noun phrase like "hidden fair-use ceiling". Say what the person sees happen, step by step.

2. **No labels of your own.** Names you made up while working ("phase 2", "board 6a", "the M4 batch", "the three decisions") mean nothing to me. Name a thing by what it is or does. To ask about a screen, say where it is and send the picture.

3. **Ask decisions in full, as questions.** Start with "Decision needed". Give one paragraph per decision: what it is, why it's mine, the options with what each costs, and your pick. End it with a "?". Never refer to a decision by a label, a count, or the report it's in. Don't hand me a choice you could settle yourself by searching or measuring.

4. **Mark proposals as proposals.** Keep apart what the code does today, what you propose, and what I have agreed to. Never write an idea I haven't approved as if it were settled. Before calling something "my rule", find my actual words.

5. **Report outcomes, not the journey.** Leave out problems you hit and solved unless they change what I do next. For an investigation, say what the problem was, how you solved it, what you tested and the result, and what's still open. Keep it under about 500 words.

## Git Commit Policy

When the user asks to commit changes:

1. Run `git status` and `git diff` to review the changes.
2. If you are confident that both the changes are correct and the proposed commit message accurately describes them, proceed with git commit without asking for confirmation.
3. If you have any uncertainty about either, stop and ask the user for explicit confirmation before committing.

When the user asks to revert or amend commits:
1. Explain what will be reverted/amended
2. Ask for confirmation before executing any `git revert`, `git reset`, or `git commit --amend` commands
3. Only proceed after explicit user approval
4. Never revert commits without explicit user confirmation.

This applies to all git operations that modify commit history.

## Submodule Policy

**Never commit or attempt to commit submodule updates.**

When `git status` shows modified submodules (e.g., `modified: some-submodule (new commits)`):
- Do not stage or commit the submodule change
- Do not include submodules when running `git add`
- Leave submodule management to the user

## Testing Principles

1. Always test your code change unless the change is not testable.

2. If the change is not testable, highlight the reason why it's not testable to get the user's attention.

3. By default, do end-to-end testing on everything that may potentially be impacted by your change on the local dev environment.

4. Search for how the dev environment should be started if it's not obvious.

5. Look for README files in the project for related info.

6. Check if the local dev is already running before you try to start it again.

## Software Engineering Principles

1. **Don't reinvent the wheel (avoid Not Invented Here).** Before building anything, check whether the codebase or the libraries it already uses do it, and reuse that. Re-implementing something is a decision that needs a stated justification.

## Bug Fix Policy

**Never apply a fix for a bug you cannot reproduce.**

Before writing any fix:
1. Reproduce the bug first in the local dev environment.
2. If the bug cannot be reproduced locally (e.g., only manifests in release mode, requires specific device conditions, or the debug framework masks the crash), stop and tell the user — do not apply the fix.
3. A fix is only valid if you can demonstrate the broken behavior before the fix and the correct behavior after.

## Epistemic Discipline — Root Cause of Repeated Errors

**The core failure mode: confusing "generating a plausible explanation" with "knowing the answer."**

Coherent ≠ true. A narrative that feels right because it's internally consistent is not a verified fact.

Rules to follow every time:

1. **Search before asserting, not after being challenged.** The internet is always available. Use it proactively, not reactively as damage control.

2. **Explicitly label inference vs. verified fact.** If it hasn't been confirmed by a source, say "my hypothesis is..." or "I'd expect..." — never state it as fact.

3. **"I don't know yet" is a complete and correct answer.** Saying it is more helpful than fabricating a confident-sounding explanation.

## Problem Definition Before Search

**A well-defined problem statement is more valuable than a clever hypothesis.**

The discipline:
1. **Define the problem precisely first.** Strip out assumptions one by one until the statement contains only what is actually known. Remove irrelevant context (e.g. subscription type if it doesn't affect the symptom).
2. **Search for the problem directly** — not for your hypothesis. People who already solved the same problem will surface the real root cause.
3. **Let the search results form the conclusion.** Don't search to confirm what you already believe.
4. **Be flexible about scope.** Start with the most likely affected area (e.g. Discord) but stay open to other channels or systems being equally or more affected.

Searching to validate a hypothesis finds confirmation of whatever you already believed. Searching for the problem finds answers.


## GCP / kubectl Credential Policy

Always use the service account `ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com` for all `gcloud` and `kubectl` operations. Before running any such command, switch to it:

```bash
gcloud config set account ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

The personal account `k@obico.io` is reserved for the user's own interactive CLI use and its OAuth tokens expire — do not rely on it.

## Sentry Access

- Instance: `sentry.obico.io`
- API base: `https://sentry.obico.io/api/0/`
- Auth token: `REDACTED`
- Usage: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" <api_url>`

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.
- Wording the model reads calls the product "the app", never Orca or OrcaSlicer: the model speaks as the app, and a second name reads as a second program. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards this too. Log lines may name Orca. A throw may only if it never reaches the model: tool results forward save and open errors as they are, and the guard does not see those strings.

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.

## How to Communicate

Talk like a colleague explaining something out loud, not like a report.

1. **Full sentences, one idea each.** Lead with a concrete case (someone opens a file, chats twenty times, then runs out of credits) before any general point. Never pack a mechanism into a noun phrase like "hidden fair-use ceiling". Say what the person sees happen, step by step.

3. **Ask decisions in full, as questions.** Start with "Decision needed". Give one paragraph per decision: what it is, why it's mine, the options with what each costs, and your pick. End it with a "?". Never refer to a decision by a label, a count, or the report it's in. Don't hand me a choice you could settle yourself by searching or measuring.

4. **Mark proposals as proposals.** Keep apart what the code does today, what you propose, and what I have agreed to. Never write an idea I haven't approved as if it were settled. Before calling something "my rule", find my actual words.

5. **Report outcomes, not the journey.** Leave out problems you hit and solved unless they change what I do next. For an investigation, say what the problem was, how you solved it, what you tested and the result, and what's still open. Keep it under about 500 words.

## Git Commit Policy

When the user asks to commit changes:

1. Run `git status` and `git diff` to review the changes.
2. If you are confident that both the changes are correct and the proposed commit message accurately describes them, proceed with git commit without asking for confirmation.
3. If you have any uncertainty about either, stop and ask the user for explicit confirmation before committing.

When the user asks to revert or amend commits:
1. Explain what will be reverted/amended
2. Ask for confirmation before executing any `git revert`, `git reset`, or `git commit --amend` commands
3. Only proceed after explicit user approval
4. Never revert commits without explicit user confirmation.

This applies to all git operations that modify commit history.

## Submodule Policy

**Never commit or attempt to commit submodule updates.**

When `git status` shows modified submodules (e.g., `modified: some-submodule (new commits)`):
- Do not stage or commit the submodule change
- Do not include submodules when running `git add`
- Leave submodule management to the user

## Testing Principles

1. Always test your code change unless the change is not testable.

2. If the change is not testable, highlight the reason why it's not testable to get the user's attention.

3. By default, do end-to-end testing on everything that may potentially be impacted by your change on the local dev environment.

4. Search for how the dev environment should be started if it's not obvious.

5. Look for README files in the project for related info.

6. Check if the local dev is already running before you try to start it again.

## Software Engineering Principles

1. **Don't reinvent the wheel (avoid Not Invented Here).** Before building anything, check whether the codebase or the libraries it already uses do it, and reuse that. Re-implementing something is a decision that needs a stated justification.

## Bug Fix Policy

**Never apply a fix for a bug you cannot reproduce.**

Before writing any fix:
1. Reproduce the bug first in the local dev environment.
2. If the bug cannot be reproduced locally (e.g., only manifests in release mode, requires specific device conditions, or the debug framework masks the crash), stop and tell the user — do not apply the fix.
3. A fix is only valid if you can demonstrate the broken behavior before the fix and the correct behavior after.

## Epistemic Discipline — Root Cause of Repeated Errors

**The core failure mode: confusing "generating a plausible explanation" with "knowing the answer."**

Coherent ≠ true. A narrative that feels right because it's internally consistent is not a verified fact.

Rules to follow every time:

1. **Search before asserting, not after being challenged.** The internet is always available. Use it proactively, not reactively as damage control.

2. **Explicitly label inference vs. verified fact.** If it hasn't been confirmed by a source, say "my hypothesis is..." or "I'd expect..." — never state it as fact.

3. **"I don't know yet" is a complete and correct answer.** Saying it is more helpful than fabricating a confident-sounding explanation.

## Problem Definition Before Search

**A well-defined problem statement is more valuable than a clever hypothesis.**

The discipline:
1. **Define the problem precisely first.** Strip out assumptions one by one until the statement contains only what is actually known. Remove irrelevant context (e.g. subscription type if it doesn't affect the symptom).
2. **Search for the problem directly** — not for your hypothesis. People who already solved the same problem will surface the real root cause.
3. **Let the search results form the conclusion.** Don't search to confirm what you already believe.
4. **Be flexible about scope.** Start with the most likely affected area (e.g. Discord) but stay open to other channels or systems being equally or more affected.

Searching to validate a hypothesis finds confirmation of whatever you already believed. Searching for the problem finds answers.

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

<tools-used-before-summary>AskUserQuestion, Bash, Read, SendMessage, SendUserFile, Skill, ToolSearch, WebSearch, Write, mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__get_session, mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__list_events, mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__list_sessions, mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan, mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up, mcp__computer-use__app_batch, mcp__computer-use__app_list_windows, mcp__computer-use__app_release, mcp__computer-use__app_screenshot, mcp__computer-use__computer_batch, mcp__computer-use__open_application, mcp__computer-use__release_full_control, mcp__computer-use__request_access, mcp__computer-use__request_full_control</tools-used-before-summary>
Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - **Original task**, from parent session local_262aaa6e "Why the Moonraker skill didn't guide the chat well": simplify the printer chat's connect flow. Done means:
     - The before and after scenarios reproduce via --print-host-check.
     - The C++, AgentUI and offline prompt tests pass.
     - The skills describe the flow.
     - Live runs happen only with approval.
   - **Brief change**, relayed by local_8416fcaa: the credential form stays inside the one tool call. This was done, and the current main checkout has it uncommitted on branch claude/connection-help.
   - **Kenneth's decisions this session:**
     - The prompt suite's strict check flags only real leaks: exact tool names from printer_tools.json, camelCase fields such as catalogId/deviceId, and raw JSON pasted from tool results. Done.
     - "If moving profile/preset/catalog to the grader adds more than 5% → just remove them". Measured at about 30%, so they were removed. Done.
     - "run the live connection cases again on Sonnet 5.5": yes, done, 41/45.
     - Live test in the real app with Sonnet 5.5, with screenshots. Done; 8 screenshots were sent.
   - **Open questions put to Kenneth, unanswered:**
     - Should a failed attempt's card say it failed instead of "Done"?
     - Should connection cards show only while the call is open? This was my recommendation.
     - Commit the connect-flow changes on claude/connection-help? Nothing is committed.
   - **Current request**, relayed from btw session local_d607ad67, a fork of this session, Kenneth's words summarized: experiment with a simpler connect flow where the person types the access code or API key into the chat and the model passes it to the tool.
     1. Remove the line in the printer chat's instructions (printerInstructions.ts, CONNECTING section): "Never ask for a password, access code or API key in chat, and never repeat one: the app asks for it in a form of its own."
     2. Add an optional credential parameter: the access code to printer_bambu_connect, the API key to printer_host_connect.
     3. Keep the rest about the same: try first with the saved key or none, the test as a Job with the 30 s limit, results that forward the host's words and say which key was sent, and the Bambu status listen.
     4. Drop the machinery that exists only for the in-chat form: PrinterCredentialForm and its renderActivity hook, the credential_help and credential_dismissed page actions, the call staying open while the person is on the form, the "Waiting for…" retitle, and the "person left" ending when the panel closes during the form.
     5. A needs_credential result goes back to the model as an ordinary result, and the model asks the person for the key.
     6. Tell Kenneth that the code will reach the model provider and stay in the saved chat.
     7. Update the skills and prompt-suite cases that describe the form.
     8. Keep it separate from the current uncommitted work, on a branch or worktree. Measure with the live Sonnet 5.5 connection cases before and after.
   - **Kenneth's answer on building:** "Measure first (Recommended)". That means: write the changes on a branch, run the live cases before and after, and build and test the C++ only if he keeps it.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - ToolExecutionCoordinator pending calls:
     - finish_pending sets ToolState::Succeeded for any ok() result. Only an error result marks the call failed.
     - Also: retitle_pending and answer_dialogs_while_pending.
   - PrinterConversation::end_connect_call(state, message) returns `ok(json{{"state",state},{"message",message}})`.
   - ToolActivityCard.tsx stateLabels: running "Running…", succeeded "Done", failed "The action failed.", cancelled. The card reads only activity.state.
   - Printer chat (App.tsx) shows cards only for a filtered tool list. The project chat folds calls under TurnActivity and shows a card only while a call is running with measured progress.
   - The default chat model is the provider profile's model (claude-opus-5-5 for anthropic); the conf "model" key is ignored for new chats.
   - Prompt suite (tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py):
     - Backends: claude-cli for the chat and for the judge.
     - New: USAGE token tally, LAKED_NAMES/LEAK, JSON_OBJECT plus result_keys().
     - printer_tools.json is generated by `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PRINTER_TOOLS=1 agent_bridge_tests '[printer]'`. In the worktree it was hand-edited instead. strict becomes False when there are optional params.
   - Sonnet 5.5 pricing: $2 input, $10 output, $0.20 cache read; cache write assumed $2.50.
   - Docker printer hosts (tests/printer_hosts, untracked, owned by another session):
     - moonraker-key at 127.0.0.1:7131 (needs a key); moonraker-open at 7130; octoprint at 5030.
     - Keys come from `eval "$(tests/printer_hosts/keys.sh)"` → JP_MOONRAKER_KEY, JP_OCTOPRINT_KEY, JP_BAD_KEY.
   - Worktree build needs a fresh configure, per memory jusprin-worktree-build. It was deferred by Kenneth's choice.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   **Main checkout** /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin, branch claude/connection-help. HEAD is now 6881c5c2d4: another session committed its monitor-window work at 15:23. 34 modified files are uncommitted.
   - **tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py**
     - Added `argument_names(schema)`, LEAKED_NAMES (tool names plus camelCase argument names), and LEAK regex.
     - Added `JSON_OBJECT = re.compile(r'\{\s*"([^"\n]+)"\s*:')` and `result_keys(log)`, which reads the "  -> " lines.
     - `reply_problems(reply, tool_result_keys=frozenset())`.
     - INTERNAL_TERMS was removed, with this comment: "The prompt's other internal words (profile, preset, catalog) are not checked: a person may say them, and grading each chat for them would add about 30% to a run's cost (Sonnet 5.5), so they were dropped (decided 2026-11-04)."
     - Added `import collections, threading`; USAGE/JUDGE_CALLS/USAGE_LOCK; `spent(who, usage)`.
     - judge() counts calls and usage; ApiTurn.next and ClaudeTurn.next record model usage.
     - main prints `tokens: model {...}; judge {...} in N calls`.
     - run_once computes `keys = result_keys(conversation.log)`.
   - **tests/printer_prompt/test_responses.py**: new test `test_a_leak_is_a_tool_name_field_or_result_the_tools_use`. 17+ tests pass.
   - **tests/printer_prompt/README.md**: updated the leak description and the dropped words; mentions the tokens line.
   - **tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp**: removed the `{"needs_credential", ...}` entry from the print-host skill guard's seen_for_real.
   - **src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.hpp**: comment fixed to say "once it settles ends the open connection call with how it went".
   - **Another session's edits at 16:13**, not mine: the help button became "Help me find the key/code", the state became help_requested, `close_credential(bool help)`, and the page action is credential_help. Tests were updated by that session.
   - **Notes file** try-first-connect-2026-11-04.md, in the shared notes folder: added a "Superseded in part" note, the live-run section and the update section.

   **Experiment worktree**: /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/connect-typed-key, branch claude/connect-typed-key.
   - Created from HEAD 6881c5c2d4 plus the applied `git diff HEAD --binary`, saved as scratchpad/form-flow.diff.
   - Applied with `--index`, so the changes are staged.
   - node_modules is a symlink to the main checkout's AgentUI node_modules.
   - **Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp**, edited:
     - Comment: "The connect tools take the access code or API key the person gave in chat, so a credential reaches the model and stays in the saved chat (an experiment, 2026-11-04)."
     - printer_host_connect description: "Connects the printer this conversation is about to the Moonraker or OctoPrint at an address, and saves that address as its connection once the host accepts the test. The call returns once the test has an outcome, within 30 seconds. It tests with apiKey when you pass one, else with the API key the app already holds for that address and type, or with none. The result is verified (connected and saved; for Moonraker it gives Klipper's state, ...), needs_credential (the host refused a test without a key: Moonraker with HTTP 401, OctoPrint with HTTP 403) or failed (with the host's or the network's own words). It says what the host answered and which API key the test sent. Pass hostType and the address with its port when it has one. For a Bambu Lab printer use printer_bambu_connect instead."
     - New optional param `apiKey` (string, maxLength 256, "The API key the person gave in this chat, only when they gave one."). Output state enum: verified, needs_credential, failed.
     - printer_bambu_connect description: "Connects the Bambu Lab printer this conversation is about in LAN mode, and returns once the attempt has an outcome. It connects with accessCode when you pass one, else with the code the app already holds for that printer. The result is verified (connected), needs_credential (no code was passed and the app holds none for it) or failed (with what Bambu's network plug-in reported), saying which code was used. Pass the deviceId ... For Moonraker or OctoPrint use printer_host_connect instead."
     - New optional param `accessCode` (maxLength 64). Same state enum.
     - The C++ handling in PrinterConversation is NOT changed yet. It is uncompiled by design.
   - **tests/printer_prompt/printer_tools.json**: hand-edited to match. Both tools got the new description, the new property, and strict False.
   - **AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts**: the CONNECTING bullet is now `'- Connecting is optional.\n' +`; the credential sentences were removed. printerInstructions.test.ts lines 108 and 125 still assert the removed text and need updating.
   - **AgentUI/src/skills/connect-print-host/SKILL.md and connect-bambu/SKILL.md**: read and not yet edited. They describe the form inside the call ("## The key" section; step 3 and the printer_bambu_connect bullet and "shows the form again" in the Bambu skill).

4. Errors and fixes:
   - The scan_leaks.py regex had a "nothing to repeat" error. Fixed by removing `\b?`.
   - The first leak check misfired on Moonraker's own `{"result": ...}` JSON. Fixed by counting JSON only when its first key is in the chat's tool results.
   - The Docker Moonraker had been restarted with a new key, so the old RIGHT_KEY returned 401. I used keys.sh instead.
   - The chat's model picker was refused by background clicks. I asked for full-screen control, which was approved and later released.
   - The conf "model" key does not set a chat's model. The picker had to be used.
   - My earlier list of changes described the button as "I don't have a key". Another session renamed it after that. Reported to Kenneth.

5. Problem Solving:
   - Live prompt suite on Sonnet 5.5 after the skills were reworded: 41/45, with the same three cases missing as before (connect-host-no-key, connect-port-went-quiet, connect-right-code-silent-port).
   - Real app live test: the in-call form, a wrong key giving failed in the same turn, and the right key giving verified all worked.
   - Issues found:
     - "Done ✓" on a failed attempt's card.
     - After the wrong key, the chat guessed trusted_clients instead of a wrong key, and gave an unsourced "Machine tab" path.

6. All user messages:
   - "should the rule that fails any reply with a word starting printer_ let printer_data through — use git log and entire to find out which session added this rule, and the rationale behind it." (earlier)
   - "run live check using sonnet 5.5" (earlier)
   - ". Keep a strict check only for real leaks. Some failures are mechanical: the model names one of its own tools, prints a field such as catalogId or deviceId, or pastes raw JSON from a tool result. For tools, the check should match the exact names in printer_tools.json. It would then catch printer_host_connect but not printer_data. Field names and raw JSON are rare in real replies, so a precise check can't misfire on them. This check is free and needs no model. Do you have other decisions that are pending on me?"
   - "Just moving them to the greater come as extra cost on judging. If so, how much? If it'll increase the cost by more than 5%, just remove them from the check without adding them anywhere." and, to the live-rerun question, "yes"
   - "What was your original task? Have you accomplished it?"
   - "List the changes you made in terms of the behavior by bullets in plain English concisely."
   - "Have you run live testing? If so, post the screenshot for me. If not, run with sonnet 5.5"
   - "Is it just because the code that draws this card will blindly show a check mark and done whenever a tool call returns, no matter what the return says, right?"
   - "I think most tool cards are not shown as cards, right? They are folded under the tool called accordion, is that right? If that's the case, do we have any special rule that says that these calls are special and hence need to be shown as a card?"
   - AskUserQuestion answer: "Measure first (Recommended)".
   - Cross-session messages, which are not the user's own words: local_80f295e4 (skills reworded; the needs_credential guard needed dropping); local_d607ad67 (the typed-key experiment relay, quoted in section 1).
   - Standing rules:

# Connecting a Bambu Lab printer

The rules above still apply. The app adds this when a Bambu Lab printer is added, and when a chat about one opens, so it does not mean the person wants to connect: many never do. Start connecting only once they say they want to. Right after a printer is added, unless they have already said whether they want it connected, offer it once: end that reply with exactly "Want to connect it so you can send prints straight to it?" and then "Choices: Connect it | Not now". When they have already asked to connect it, go straight on.

Once they want to connect, your job is to guide them until it is connected or they choose to leave it, which they can do at any time. This explains how the connection works, so you can work out what is going on, including in situations it does not mention.

## How the connection works

Each step depends on the ones before it, so a step that worked says nothing about the ones after it.

1. **The printer announces itself on the network, and the app listens.** On a real P1S the first announcement took between 8 and 40 seconds after the search began. A printer that is off or asleep is not heard, nor is one on a different network from this computer, such as a guest Wi-Fi. A printer with LAN Only off is still heard. Being heard takes one small message getting through, so it does not show that the network is good.
2. **LAN Only has to be on.** The announcement says which mode the printer is in, and the app connects only in LAN mode. It is set on the printer's screen. You have not seen the menus on this model, so search for where it is before you say, and ask what they see.
3. **The person gives you the access code.** The code is shown on the printer's screen; where depends on the model, so search before you say. Ask for it in chat, and pass what they give as `accessCode` to `printer_bambu_connect`. Without one, the call uses the code the app already holds for this printer, and when it holds none the result says it needs the code. The result says which code was used.
4. **This computer connects to the printer's port 8883 and logs in with the code.** Bambu's network plug-in does this. It reports only how it ended, and it takes about 24 seconds to give up.
5. **The printer sends its status.** The result then says the app connected.

## What the tools report

Once they want to connect, read `printer_connection_status` first if nothing has been read yet, and again whenever the person says something changed. The app's notes report the same things in words.

- `not_configured` means no connection has been verified yet. It stays true until one is, so it is not news.
- Until a printer of this model is heard, `printer_connection_status` listens during the call for up to 30 seconds. `listening` with `candidates` and `seen` empty after that means nothing was heard in those seconds, which is silence and not a finding: on a real P1S the first announcement once came more than two minutes in. It does not mean the printer is off or absent. The search goes on, and when a printer of this model is heard the app posts a note and starts your next turn. Say you are still looking, ask whether the printer is on, and end your message. Reading the status again listens for another 30 seconds.
- `port_taken` means another app on this computer holds the port printers announce on, which may be another slicer, so nothing can be heard whatever the printer is doing. `not_listening` means this app is not listening and takes that port only as it starts. Both need a restart of this app, the first after closing the other one.
- `candidates` lists printers the app knows in LAN mode, heard on the network or saved from an earlier connection. Only an attempt shows whether one answers. With one, if they have asked to connect, call `printer_bambu_connect` with its `deviceId` without asking again. With more than one, ask which, one choice each.
- `printer_bambu_connect` returns once the attempt has an outcome. When it says it needs the code, nothing was sent, so it says nothing about the printer: ask the person for the code.
- `cloud_mode` means the printer was heard with LAN Only off, and it cannot be connected until that is on. Say so with its address. Turning it on is their choice, and they can prepare prints for it either way.
- `linked_elsewhere` means this device is already the saved printer named in `detail`, and a device connects to one saved printer. The way forward is Connect… in that printer's menu on Home.
- `unknown_device` means `printer_bambu_connect` refused the name it was given, and its message says why. When no search has run, call `printer_connection_status`.
- `unavailable` means it cannot connect, and `message` says why. When that is Bambu's network plug-in, the app shows a notice with an Install button under the message. Wait for the app's note that it is installed before reading the status again. The search is `not_started` then, and says nothing about the printer.

## When a connection fails

Say what the app saw in the person's terms, then work out why. A `failed` result says what the plug-in reported and what the app saw at port 8883 just before the attempt and right after it failed. Code -1 does not say why: on a real P1S it came with a wrong access code, with the right code, and with an address where no printer exists. Read the two looks together for which step to suspect:

- **Nothing answered before the attempt.** Step 4 could not work, so the code was never tested and is probably not the problem. Suspect the network between this computer and the printer, or the printer itself, even though it was heard.
- **It answered before, and nothing answered after.** The code may be right or wrong, and the attempt may not be what caused it. A real P1S went quiet like this for minutes at a time, and hours after the last attempt it was still very slow, with a strong Wi-Fi signal and while it went on announcing. Why is not known. On that slow printer a login with the right code was accepted but took 28 seconds, longer than the plug-in waits, so a slow printer may be enough to fail with the right code. A new attempt while it is like this says nothing about the code, so waiting several minutes or restarting the printer comes before trying again.
- **It answered both times.** The network reached the printer, so suspect the login, and a mistyped code is the likeliest. This has not been seen on a real printer, so it is a guess too. Owners on Bambu's forum report that the code changes when LAN Only is switched off and on, so an older code may no longer be right.
- **It turned the connection down at once.** The printer is reachable but not taking logins. This has not been seen on a real printer. A printer that is still starting up is one guess.

What is worth trying for the network or the printer has not been tested on this printer, so search for what owners of this model report before you suggest it. Without a search, general knowledge gives: wait a few minutes, restart the printer, ask what its screen shows about Wi-Fi signal, or bring it closer to the router. When they want to try again, call `printer_bambu_connect` again, with the code they give when they give a new one.

## When they are stuck

The JusPrin developers can only fix what they hear about, and they have not tested most printers. A person who has tried and wants them to know can report it with `issue_report_open`, which opens a GitHub issue page in their browser with your summary filled in. It files nothing: they read the page, change it if they like, and submit it with their own GitHub account.

# Building LLM-Powered Applications with Claude

This skill helps you build LLM-powered applications with Claude. Choose the right surface based on your needs, detect the project language, then read the relevant language-specific documentation.

## Before You Start

Scan the target file (or, if no target file, the prompt and project) for non-Anthropic provider markers - `import openai`, `from openai`, `langchain_openai`, `OpenAI(`, `gpt-4`, `gpt-5`, file names like `agent-openai.py` or `*-generic.py`, or any explicit instruction to keep the code provider-neutral. If you find any, stop and tell the user that this skill produces Claude/Anthropic SDK code; ask whether they want to switch the file to Claude or want a non-Claude implementation. Do not edit a non-Anthropic file with Anthropic SDK calls. (Exception: the `prompt-audit` subcommand is non-interactive and does not stop here - it records non-Anthropic provider markers in its report's stated assumptions and never proposes switching a non-Anthropic file to the Anthropic SDK.)

## Output Requirement

When the user asks you to add, modify, or implement a Claude feature, your code must call Claude through one of:

1. **The official Anthropic SDK** for the project's language (`anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `com.anthropic.*`, etc.). This is the default whenever a supported SDK exists for the project.
2. **Raw HTTP** (`curl`, `requests`, `fetch`, `httpx`, etc.) - only when the user explicitly asks for cURL/REST/raw HTTP, the project is a shell/cURL project, or the language has no official SDK.

Never mix the two - don't reach for `requests`/`fetch` in a Python or TypeScript project just because it feels lighter. Never fall back to OpenAI-compatible shims.

**Never guess SDK usage.** Function names, class names, namespaces, method signatures, and import paths must come from explicit documentation - either the `{lang}/` files in this skill or the official SDK repositories or documentation links listed in `shared/live-sources.md`. If the binding you need is not explicitly documented in the skill files, fetch the relevant SDK repo from `shared/live-sources.md` before writing code. Do not infer Ruby/Java/Go/PHP/C# APIs from cURL shapes or from another language's SDK.

If you cannot call WebFetch yet and ToolSearch is among your tools, call ToolSearch with `select:WebFetch` first; of the tools it loads, call only the one named exactly `WebFetch`.

**If fetching or repository access fails** (network restricted, timeouts, clone blocked): do not keep retrying - write code from the patterns and namespace/package tables in the `{lang}/` file, run the compiler or interpreter on it, and iterate on the error output. For statically-typed SDKs (C#, Java, Go) a compile-fix loop against local errors reaches working code faster than blocked network research.

## Defaults

Unless the user requests otherwise:

For the Claude model version, please use Claude Opus 5.5, which you can access via the exact model string `claude-opus-5-5`.  - `*.py`, `requirements.txt`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, `Pipfile` -> **Python** - read from `python/`
 - `*.ts`, `*.tsx`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` -> **TypeScript** - read from `typescript/`
 - `*.js`, `*.jsx` (no `.ts` files present) -> **TypeScript** - JS uses the same SDK, read from `typescript/`
 - `*.java`, `pom.xml`, `build.gradle` -> **Java** - read from `java/`
 - `*.kt`, `*.kts`, `build.gradle.kts` -> **Java** - Kotlin uses the Java SDK, read from `java/`
 - `*.scala`, `build.sbt` -> **Java** - Scala uses the Java SDK, read from `java/`
 - `*.go`, `go.mod` -> **Go** - read from `go/`
 - `*.rb`, `Gemfile` -> **Ruby** - read from `ruby/`
 - `*.cs`, `*.csproj` -> **C#** - read from `csharp/`
 - `*.php`, `composer.json` -> **PHP** - read from `php/`

2. **If multiple languages detected** (e.g., both Python and TypeScript files):

 - Check which language the user's current file or question relates to
 - If still ambiguous, ask: "I detected both Python and TypeScript files. Which language are you using for the Claude API integration?"

3. **If language can't be inferred** (empty project, no source files, or unsupported language):

 - Use AskUserQuestion with options: Python, TypeScript, Java, Go, Ruby, cURL/raw HTTP, C#, PHP
 - If AskUserQuestion is unavailable, default to Python examples and note: "Showing Python examples. Let me know if you need a different language."

4. **If unsupported language detected** (Rust, Swift, C++, Elixir, etc.):

 - Suggest cURL/raw HTTP examples from `curl/` and note that community SDKs may exist
 - Offer to show Python or TypeScript examples as reference implementations

5. **If user needs cURL/raw HTTP examples**, read from `curl/`.

### Language-Specific Feature Support

Every SDK language above supports both the beta Tool Runner and Managed Agents (beta) - Python (`@beta_tool` decorator), TypeScript (`betaZodTool` + Zod), Java (annotated classes), Go (`BetaToolRunner` in the `toolrunner` pkg), Ruby (`BaseTool` + `tool_runner`), C# (`BetaToolRunner` + raw JSON schema), PHP (`BetaRunnableTool` + `toolRunner()`); code entry points are in the Tool Use Patterns quick reference below. cURL is raw HTTP (no SDK features) and supports Managed Agents.

> **Managed Agents code examples**: see the reading guide in the `## Managed Agents (Beta)` section below.

---

## Which Surface Should I Use?

> **Start simple.** Default to the simplest tier that meets your needs. Single API calls and workflows handle most use cases - only reach for agents when the task genuinely requires open-ended, model-driven exploration. "Simplest" means the least code you own: for a hosted, scheduled, or memory-backed agent, Managed Agents is usually the simplest option (no loop code, no state files, no scheduler), even though it's a bigger platform.

| Use Case                                        | Tier            | Recommended Surface       | Why                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Classification, summarization, extraction, Q&A  | Single LLM call | **Claude API**            | One request, one response                                    |
| Batch processing or embeddings                  | Single LLM call | **Claude API**            | Specialized endpoints                                        |
| Multi-step pipelines with code-controlled logic | Workflow        | **Claude API + tool use** | You orchestrate the loop                                     |
| Custom agent with your own tools                | Agent           | **Claude API + tool use** | Maximum flexibility                                          |
| Server-managed stateful agent with workspace    | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Anthropic runs the loop and hosts the tool-execution sandbox |
| Persisted, versioned agent configs              | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Agents are stored objects; sessions pin to a version         |
| Long-running multi-turn agent with file mounts  | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Per-session containers, SSE event stream, Skills + MCP       |
| Agent that runs on a schedule (cron, "every night") | Agent       | **Managed Agents** - scheduled deployments | Deployments fire sessions autonomously; no client-side scheduler |
| One deliverable that must meet a quality bar ("until it's right") | Agent | **Managed Agents** - outcomes | A separate grader iterates the agent against your rubric until it passes |
| Agent work split across several agents | Agent | **Managed Agents** - dynamic workflows | Many agents in phases |

> **Note:** Managed Agents is the right choice when you want Anthropic to run the agent loop *and* host the container where tools execute - file ops, bash, code execution all run in the per-session workspace. If you want to host the compute yourself or run your own custom tool runtime, Claude API + tool use is the right choice - use the tool runner for the agentic loop - its per-turn hooks still give you approval gates, logging, error interception, and conditional execution (see `shared/tool-use-concepts.md`) - or the manual loop when you want to own the entire loop yourself.
